answer: Another defense is liability vouching: a new agent can only trade after established agents vouch for it, and a voucher loses reputation or stake if its vouchee cheats. A sybil operator can mint many names, but each needs a credible voucher, and one exposed cluster burns the whole chain. Like pigment that cannot hide in a spiral pattern, or a lone knoll that stands out on flat ground, forged clusters become visible because their vouching graph is dense, circular, and disconnected from real participants.
